newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy February new car sales seen higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy February new car sales seen higher.

text.p: Italian new car registrations in February are set to see around a 20 percent rise to nearly 200,000 units compared to February 1996 helped by the government's car buying incentive scheme started in January.
The Ministry of Transport will publish official Italian February new car registration figures on Monday March 10.

Forecaster Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) says the outlook continues to be good, and according to preliminary data car orders for February should have shown a bigger increase than the 33 percent rise seen for orders in Italy during January.
For January 1997, Italian car registrations rose 4.38 percent on the year to 207,000 units. In February 1996, new car registrations reached 162,982.

At the end of last month, Italian carmaker Fiat Auto said their January orders had risen 35/40 percent. The group added that due to strikes by metalworkers in this month production had been reduced by around 10,000 units.

"I have a rise of around 20 percent to around 200,000 registrations," said Giampaolo Trasi, analyst at brokers IMI Segeco. He pointed out that February registrations will gain from the incentive scheme and also a recovery from the strike-hit month of January.
CSP Director Gianprimo Quagliano sees a double digit percentage rise in registrations in February due to the incentive scheme while Ilaria Fornari at JP Morgan sees a rise in excess of 10 percent.

The Italian government introduced its car buying scheme in January to run to the end of September, whereby owners of cars older than 10-years old can receive price discounts if they trade their old cars to buy new ones.
